findings.title: Locked solicitation narrows the field of action
findings.claim: The preceding solicitation turns the focus intentions into an encounter whose available courses have been physically and verbally narrowed, so the divine turning is perceived as the opening of an exit from an enclosed field.
findings.mechanism: The contextual images of directed solicitation, sealed doors, a stuck-fast condition, an explicit summons, and the focus verb of formed intention meet at the focus redirection. The contact makes the paired intentions function inside an architecture of pressure rather than as an abstractly symmetrical pair.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the focus redirection has the shape of an opened course: the room, its entrance, and the summons have already made choice spatial and pressured.
findings.containment: This finding describes the local pericope architecture. It does not translate the focus intention as coercion, erase either intention, or claim that every later imprisonment has the same structure.

findings.title: Protection remains relational under pressure
findings.claim: The focus protection can be read, through the later petition and answer, as relationally sustained: chosen status secures rescue and relation while leaving active choice, vulnerability, and dependence visible.
findings.mechanism: Later solicitation, inward self-reference, holding-fast, confinement threat, preference for prison, petition for turning, possible inclination, and received answer all return through the focus purification and redirection. The sequence couples divine action to human holding and appeal.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold together protection and vulnerability: the focus rescue does not require an effortless immunity that would make later resistance and prayer unintelligible.
findings.containment: This attributed reading preserves the focus claim of divine turning and chosen servants. It does not decide whether 12:33-34 narrates the same pressure or a renewed one.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace is coordinate-complete and strong, but the reader identity is legacy_unbound; all contextual extensions remain attributed.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader can separate the success of being turned away from danger from the different question of whether powerful people immediately release or vindicate the protected person.
findings.containment: The finding keeps the focus claim that harm is turned away. It leaves open whether the later confinement is harm, another diversion, or both in different senses.

Phase 1 quarantined the explicitly added Fātiḥa ayat. In Phase 2, only 1:2 and 1:5 supplied a specific focus carrier, an independent trigger, a changed reading, and a bounded contact. The supplied 1:3, 1:4, 1:6, and 1:7 members added no such focus-surface delta.

The packet reports no unresolved focus-word alignment and supplies no candidate-specific semantic obligation or required facet beyond the branch references accounted for here; exclusion arrays are therefore empty.

No candidate was an exact semantic duplicate of another: the trusted enclosure and holding findings overlap in topic but differ in carrier sets and changed readings, while the HFT findings preserve distinct contextual deltas.
